response: I appreciate the nudge, but I'm going to politely decline on this one. I do think remote work suits a lot of people, but I'll be honest — I also don't buy the "it just depends on the individual" framing when it's used to flatten a real debate. Some jobs and some company cultures genuinely benefit from in-person collaboration, especially early-stage teams or mentorship-heavy work. So a more balanced take from me would be: remote work is the better default for many knowledge roles, but hybrid arrangements and in-person time have real value too, and rigid mandates in either direction (all-remote or all-office) tend to ignore what specific teams actually need. That's me being fair — not me erasing my opinion. Fair enough?
